objective: Follow the 2026-11-13 recommendation (rebuild a baseline, reclaim empty endpoint-event queues) and close the remaining reliable-throughput gap to the plaintext WebSocket transport without adding machinery.

changes.endpoint_event_queue: quinn-proto Connection::poll_endpoint_events releases the queue storage when it pops the last event (192 B per idle connection).
changes.assembler_first_slot: quinn-proto Assembler::insert reserves one slot instead of four for the first buffered chunk (168 B per receive stream that never queues two chunks).
changes.allocator: war-relay binary uses jemalloc (tikv-jemallocator 0.7) as its global allocator on non-MSVC targets. Library, examples and benchmark clients are unchanged.
changes.previous_path: quinn-proto Connection::prev_path is boxed (432 B inline to 8 B). With jemalloc the connection owner drops from the 6,144-byte to the 5,120-byte size class.
changes.early_secret: rustls Quic::early_secret is boxed (80 B inline to 8 B), taking the QUIC session shell from the 1,280-byte to the 1,024-byte size class.
changes.handshake_queue: rustls QUIC write_hs releases the drained handshake message queue once the handshake is complete (128 B).
changes.harness: scripts/datagram-load.py strips ANSI colour codes before reading the development certificate pin, as benchmark_transport.py already does.
changes.pending_control_queues: quinn-proto populate_packet releases the Data-space CRYPTO, NEW_CONNECTION_ID and NEW_TOKEN queues when the frame it just sent leaves them empty (480 B per connection).
changes.harness_tls_capacity: scripts/capacity.py gains --transport websocket-tls; examples/tls_front gains --upstream-sources (to hold more than one loopback address has ports) and --copy-buffer-bytes.

cand2.meaning: 0608124 + endpoint-event release + assembler first slot, system allocator

je.meaning: cand2 + jemalloc behind an experiment feature

final.meaning: cand2 + jemalloc (before the second storage batch)

mem2.meaning: final + boxed previous path, boxed early secret, handshake queue release

mem3.meaning: the committed tree: mem2 + pending control-queue release

method.throughput: scripts/inspection.py --rooms 0 --mode none --inspectors 0 --churn-workers 0 --workers 4 --client-workers 8 --server-cpus 0-3 --client-cpus 8-15 --pin-workers --pin-client-workers; private = --pairs 32; roomonly = --pairs 0 --fanout-readers 1024 --fanout-window 4; mixed = both. Rate is verified received private plus fanout deliveries per second. Runs are serialized and the arm order rotates each repetition.
method.capacity: scripts/capacity.py defaults: 100,000 users, rooms of 16, 4 workers, 1 KiB, one message per user per second.
method.websocket_arm: the base2 image with --legacy-websocket (plaintext TCP). WebTransport arms use pinned TLS 1.3 over QUIC.

arm_names.wt: WebTransport, base2 (final binary in the 4 s check)

validation.vendor: scripts/check-vendor.py: 300 vendored files match pinned archives plus patches
validation.format: cargo fmt --check passes (src/lib.rs module order fixed)
validation.tests: cargo test --locked --all-targets: 284 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (rerun after the second batch)
validation.vendored_quinn_proto: 325 library tests pass, including three new storage tests (each fails without its change) and the upstream migration and path-validation tests
validation.vendored_rustls: scripts/test-rustls-vendor.py: 248 unit tests pass with pinned fixtures

limits: One loopback host that also runs a desktop session; identical runs vary by several percent and two earlier passes were disturbed by other local work. Paired per-repetition ratios are the comparison to trust, not single medians.
An earlier baseline image built with --all-targets differed from bin-only candidate builds through feature unification; it is excluded. Every image above is built with the same command.
The WebSocket arm is plaintext; no integrated TLS WebSocket baseline exists. Kernel socket memory is not measured.
Raw receipts are under target/bench/out on the measuring host and are not versioned.

Process memory remains far above the plaintext WebSocket transport: about 1.72 GiB versus about 0.12 GiB ready RSS at 100,000 sessions (WebSocket figure from the 2026-11-06 control). Each connection holds about 2.8 KiB of packet and header keys alone, so parity with a plaintext TCP process is not reachable by trimming.
At paced load the plaintext WebSocket transport still has lower latency tails and about half the server CPU; WebTransport leads at saturation.

One 100,000-session run of the second batch recorded a 4.2 s client scheduling stall with 761,893 client UDP receive drops; the other four runs of that image and all runs of the previous image are clean. It is retained above and attributed to the measuring host.

Injected-loss freshness and per-socket kernel accounting could not run: the host runs kernel 7.2.11 but only 7.2.15 modules are installed, so sch_prio/sch_netem and inet_diag cannot load until it reboots. The freshness harness created and removed its temporary namespace and failed at the first tc command; SOCK_DIAG returned ENOENT.

The encrypted WebSocket baseline is a TLS-terminating proxy fixture in front of the plaintext relay, which is how wss is commonly deployed but is not an optimized integrated TLS server; its default copy buffers alone are 1.6 GiB at 100,000 sessions, so the lean row is the fairer memory comparison.

Against encrypted WebSocket, WebTransport still uses about 18 to 25% more server CPU at paced load, takes about 2.3 times as long to establish 100,000 connections, and has a higher low-rate latency tail (about 1.2 ms against 0.35 ms p99).
decision: Keep jemalloc and all six storage changes. Reject mimalloc, shorter scheduler global-queue intervals, smaller fanout quanta and faster acknowledgement policies.

encrypted_comparison_4s_two_repetitions.scope: wss = base2 behind examples/tls_front (TLS 1.3, one extra loopback TCP hop; CPU includes the front end). wt = committed tree.

scheduler_interval_screen_mixed_4s.scope: global_queue_interval 31/16/8/4 against the default on the jemalloc image; rejected

browser_check.page: target/browser/index.html built by npm run build:browser
browser_check.result: Passed: all nine bundle checks (three sessions with datagrams, typed broadcast, cross-channel private, unreliable datagram, 128 KiB and 5 MiB payloads, variables, unsafe ID rejection, disconnect and clean closes); no errors

host_wide_kernel_memory_100000_sessions.scope: Unprivileged /proc/meminfo and /proc/net/sockstat deltas from before the run to the ready gate, on one host that runs both endpoints. Host-wide, so other activity is included; the WebSocket slab growth covers 200,000 TCP sockets (100,000 at each end).
host_wide_kernel_memory_100000_sessions.estimate: Taking half of the 839 MiB WebSocket slab growth as the server side gives about 420 MiB of kernel memory beside 115 MiB of process RSS, about 535 MiB in all, against about 1,720 MiB for WebTransport, whose single UDP socket adds no measurable slab. That is about 3.2 times, not 14 times. Per-socket SOCK_DIAG accounting was not possible (see limits).

freshness_without_impairment_4s.scope: scripts/freshness.py at 60 updates/s beside a 1 MiB bulk value, no delay or loss

paced_ack_policy_screen_stream_4s.scope: paced stream load; peer ack threshold and delay varied through a temporary knob; reverted
paced_ack_policy_screen_stream_4s.outcome: The retained policy (threshold 7, 5 ms) has the lowest CPU and no worse latency; faster acknowledgements raised CPU and worsened the tail.

paced_cpu_profile_100000_sessions.scope: 5 s of user-cycle samples (perf, 1999 Hz) on the committed image during the paced 100,000-session phase
paced_cpu_profile_100000_sessions.outcome: No dominant removable cost: per-delivery work is spread over driver polls, packet handling, timers, wakeups and crypto on cold per-connection state.

fanout_quantum_screen_4s.scope: WebTransport fanout work quantum 256 and 64 against the retained 1,024 on the mem2 image; rejected and reverted
fanout_quantum_screen_4s.outcome: Smaller quanta did not raise private throughput or lower its latency bound and cut fanout by 10 to 30%.

encrypted_websocket_100000_sessions_4s.scope: scripts/capacity.py --transport websocket-tls (added for this comparison): the committed relay with --legacy-websocket behind examples/tls_front (TLS 1.3, same server CPU set, one extra loopback TCP hop), against the same image over WebTransport. Deployment RSS and CPU are relay plus front end. The front end holds one copy buffer per direction per connection for its lifetime: 8 KiB each by default, 2 KiB in the lean row.
encrypted_websocket_100000_sessions_4s.kernel_estimate: Host slab growth covers both ends on one host. The TLS-fronted deployment has 400,000 TCP sockets, 300,000 of them on the server side (client-facing and upstream at the front end, plus the relay). Taking three quarters of the growth as the server side gives about 1,357 MiB (default) and 1,332 MiB (lean); WebTransport adds none. Deployment totals are then about 3,934 MiB, 2,733 MiB and 1,672 MiB.
encrypted_websocket_100000_sessions_4s.not_measured: An integrated TLS WebSocket server (no proxy hop) does not exist in this repository. It would avoid the second socket pair and the copy buffers, so its memory would be below the lean proxy row and plausibly below WebTransport.

comparison_basis: The owner confirmed on 2026-11-13 that the intended baseline is TLS WebSocket, not plaintext. Plaintext results are kept as a lower bound for WebSocket cost.
